title_en: Nongyin Financial Co., Ltd. v. Guangdong Sanxing Enterprise (Group) Company Axle Co., Ltd. — dispute over guarantee contract
ruling_gist_en: According to the provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, after a mortgage contract is confirmed invalid, the allocation of liability between the parties shall be determined according to their degree of fault. For a mortgage contract that is found invalid due to violation of Chinese laws and administrative regulations, since Chinese laws and administrative regulations are publicly available, all parties should have knowledge of the relevant provisions, and thus it should be found that all parties bear some degree of fault for the invalidity of the mortgage contract.

full_text_en:
Agricultural Bank Financial Services Limited v. Guangdong Sanxing Enterprise (Group) Company Axle Co., Ltd. — dispute over guarantee contract

【Ruling Summary】

Pursuant to the provisions of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the PRC, after a mortgage contract is confirmed void, the allocation of liability between the parties shall be determined based on their respective degrees of fault. For a mortgage contract that is invalidated due to violation of Chinese laws or administrative regulations, as such laws and regulations are publicly available, all parties concerned should have understood the relevant provisions. Therefore, it shall be determined that each party bears a certain degree of fault for the invalidity of the mortgage contract.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2004) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 23

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): Agricultural Bank Financial Services Limited, domiciled at 23/F, Tower 1, Admiralty Centre, 18 Harcourt Road, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Legal representative: Liang Zhiren, manager of the company.
Agent ad litem: Feng Cantong, lawyer of Guangdong Datong Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Zhu Yongping, lawyer of Guangdong Datong Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance): Guangdong Sanxing Enterprise (Group) Company Axle Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 2 Jianshe First Road, Yangjiang City, Guangdong Province.
Legal representative: Xie Tiguang, chairman of the board of directors.
Agent ad litem: Xu Shifang, male, Han nationality, born in 1962, residing at No. 4, Seventh Alley, Ergang Second Street, Jiangcheng District, Yangjiang City, Guangdong Province.
Agent ad litem: Huang Chengxian, lawyer of Guangdong Sanmin Law Firm.

The appellant, Agricultural Bank Financial Services Limited (hereinafter referred to as Agricultural Bank Financial), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment of the Guangdong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance) in case (2002) Yue Gao Fa Min Si Chu Zi No. 1 concerning a dispute over a guarantee contract with the respondent, Guangdong Sanxing Enterprise (Group) Company Axle Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sanxing Axle Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of presiding judge Wang Yun and acting judges Yang Xingye and Chen Jizhong, to hear the case, with Liang Ying serving as court clerk. After hearings on May 9, 2005 and February 28, 2006, with Feng Cantong, agent ad litem for Agricultural Bank Financial, and Xu Shifang and Huang Chengxian, agents ad litem for Sanxing Axle Company, appearing in court to participate in the proceedings, the case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found: Agricultural Bank Financial and Junxing Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Junxing Company) entered into four financing agreements in Hong Kong from 1995 to 1996:

1. On November 20, 1995, the parties signed the "Mortgage Loan Agreement" with reference number (95) No. 9536 of the Agricultural Bank Financial Services Limited. Pursuant to this agreement, Agricultural Bank Financial granted Junxing Company a loan with a maximum limit of USD 9,000,000, with a term of nine months from the date of drawdown. The annual interest rate was the US dollar prime rate plus 4 percentage points. If Junxing Company failed to repay the principal and interest on time, Agricultural Bank Financial would charge interest on the overdue amount at 120% of the original interest rate. The agreement was governed by the laws of Hong Kong, and both the borrower and the lender agreed to submit to the jurisdiction of the Hong Kong courts.

2. On December 15, 1995, the parties signed the "Mortgage Loan Agreement" with reference number (95) No. 9539 of the Agricultural Bank Financial Services Limited, agreeing that Agricultural Bank Financial would provide Junxing Company with a loan with a maximum limit of USD 5,000,000. The loan term, interest rate, and choice of law and jurisdiction were the same as those in the Mortgage Loan Agreement (95) No. 9536.

3. On December 15, 1995, the parties signed the "Letter of Credit Financing Mortgage Agreement" with reference number (95) No. 9525 of the Agricultural Bank Financial Services Limited, agreeing that Agricultural Bank Financial would provide Junxing Company with letter of credit issuance financing with a maximum limit of USD 7,500,000, including a trust receipt facility of USD 6,000,000. The financing term was one year from the date of signing, with the trust receipt facility term being 90 days. If the trust receipt facility was not cleared on time, additional interest would be paid at the US dollar prime rate plus 6 percentage points. The agreement was governed by the laws of Hong Kong and the mainland, and both parties agreed to submit to the jurisdiction of the Hong Kong and mainland courts.

4. On May 12, 1996, the parties signed the "Letter of Credit Financing Mortgage Agreement" with reference number (96) No. 9601 of the Agricultural Bank Financial Services Limited, agreeing that Agricultural Bank Financial would provide Junxing Company with letter of credit financing with a maximum limit of USD 8,000,000, including a trust receipt facility of USD 7,600,000. The financing term was from the date of signing to December 31, 1996, with the trust receipt facility term being 90 days. If the trust receipt facility was not cleared on time, additional interest would be paid at the US dollar prime rate plus 6 percentage points. Both parties agreed that the contract would be governed by the laws of Hong Kong and the mainland, and would submit to the jurisdiction of the Hong Kong and mainland courts.

After the above agreements were signed, Agricultural Bank Financial, in accordance with the provisions of the two Mortgage Loan Agreements, transferred the loans of USD 9,000,000 and USD 5,000,000 in three installments to the bank account designated by Junxing Company on November 29, 1995, December 22, 1995, and January 5, 1996. Junxing Company confirmed each transfer in writing. Agricultural Bank Financial adduced evidence that after the above loans matured, Junxing Company repaid interest of USD 2,481,953.43. Agricultural Bank Financial also, in accordance with the two Letter of Credit Financing Mortgage Agreements and Junxing Company's applications, from June 6, 1996 to January 6, 1997, issued ten letters of credit for Junxing Company. After deducting the margin deposits for the letters of credit, Agricultural Bank Financial actually provided Junxing Company with letter of credit financing of HKD 67,992,581.32. Regarding this financing, Agricultural Bank Financial adduced evidence that Junxing Company only repaid interest of HKD 3,529,876.39, and the remaining principal and interest remain unpaid to date.

Regarding the financing provided for under the aforementioned Mortgage Loan Agreements and Letter of Credit Financing Mortgage Agreements, Sanxing Axle Company provided guarantees as follows:

1. Both of the above Mortgage Loan Agreements provided that Sanxing Axle Company would provide as mortgage the properties on four parcels of comprehensive land located in Yangjiang City, Guangdong Province, with a total area of 122,304.44 square meters (land use certificates: Yang Fu Guo Yong (Te) Zi Nos. 95-363, 95-364, 95-365, 95-367). Although Sanxing Axle Company did not sign or seal the two agreements, it registered the mortgage of the collateral agreed upon in the two Mortgage Loan Agreements on December 19, 1995.

2. Both of the above Letter of Credit Financing Mortgage Agreements provided that Sanxing Axle Company would provide as mortgage the land use rights of the same guarantee properties agreed in the two Mortgage Loan Agreements, i.e., the four parcels of comprehensive land located in Yangjiang City under the name of Sanxing Axle Company. Additionally, the Letter of Credit Financing Mortgage Agreement (96) No. 9601 specifically added the land use rights of three parcels of comprehensive land with a total area of 81,233.91 square meters (land use certificates: Yang Fu Guo Yong Te Zi Nos. 96-459, 96-460, 96-461) located at No. 2 Jianshe First Road, Jiangcheng District, Yangjiang City, under the name of Sanxing Axle Company as collateral for this letter of credit financing. However, Sanxing Axle Company only signed and sealed the Letter of Credit Financing Mortgage Agreement (96) No. 9601. On May 23, 1996, Agricultural Bank Financial and Sanxing Axle Company registered the mortgage of the land use rights with land use certificate numbers Yang Fu Guo Yong Te Zi Nos. 96-459, 96-460, 96-461.

3. Regarding the loan debt of USD 9,000,000 owed by Junxing Company under the Mortgage Loan Agreement (95) No. 9536, Sanxing Axle Company issued an "Irrevocable Guarantee" to Agricultural Bank Financial on November 20, 1995, undertaking to provide unconditional, irrevocable, and continuing guarantee for the said debt and the interest and expenses payable when Junxing Company failed or refused to repay in accordance with the agreement.

4. Regarding the total financing of USD 21,500,000 under the two Loan Agreements and the Letter of Credit Financing Mortgage Agreement (95) No. 9525, Sanxing Axle Company issued an "Irrevocable Guarantee" on December 15, 1995, undertaking to provide unconditional, irrevocable, and continuing guarantee for the said debt and the interest and expenses payable when Junxing Company failed or refused to repay in accordance with the agreement.

5. Regarding the total financing of USD 29,500,000 under the two Mortgage Loan Agreements and the two Letter of Credit Financing Mortgage Agreements, Sanxing Axle Company issued an "Irrevocable Guarantee" to Agricultural Bank Financial on May 23, 1996, undertaking to provide unconditional, irrevocable, and continuing guarantee for the said debt and the interest and expenses payable.

The court of first instance also found: Agricultural Bank Financial is a limited company registered in Hong Kong on November 1, 1988, holding a Hong Kong money lender's license. Junxing Company is a limited company registered in Hong Kong on June 4, 1992. Sanxing Axle Company is a joint venture enterprise registered in Yangjiang City, Guangdong Province, having the status of a legal person, with its business scope covering the production, manufacture, and sale of automobile parts.

The parties to this case have no objection to the above facts found by the court of first instance.

On July 18, 1998, Agricultural Bank Financial filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, seeking a judgment ordering Sanxing Axle Company to bear joint and several liability for the debts owed by Junxing Company and to enjoy priority in payment from the land use rights provided as mortgage by Sanxing Axle Company.

On December 28, 1999, the court of first instance rendered a civil judgment (1998) Yue Fa Jing Er Chu Zi No. 8 in this case, holding that Agricultural Bank Financial had not yet pursued its claim against Junxing Company through litigation or arbitration, causing the amount of Junxing Company's unpaid debt to be unascertainable, and the scope of Sanxing Axle Company's corresponding civil compensation liability was also difficult to determine. Agricultural Bank Financial should bear the legal consequences of not filing a lawsuit or applying for arbitration against Junxing Company. The judgment dismissed Agricultural Bank Financial's claims.

Agricultural Bank Financial, dissatisfied with the above judgment, appealed to this Court. This Court, by civil ruling (2000) Jing Zhong Zi No. 91 dated December 21, 2001, remanded the case for retrial on the grounds that: Agricultural Bank Financial had not pursued its claim against the debtor Junxing Company, the amount of Junxing Company's debt to Agricultural Bank Financial that could not be recovered had not been determined, and the scope of the guarantor Sanxing Axle Company's civil compensation liability was difficult to ascertain; directly dismissing Agricultural Bank Financial's claims was procedurally unfavorable to protecting the lawful rights and interests of the parties. The court of first instance should grant Agricultural Bank Financial a reasonable period to file a lawsuit or apply for arbitration regarding the principal contract with a competent court.

The court of first instance formed a new collegial panel and retried the case under ordinary procedure. During the trial, the court of first instance informed Agricultural Bank Financial that it should file a lawsuit or apply for arbitration regarding the principal contract with a competent court to determine its claim amount against Junxing Company. On June 18, 2002, Agricultural Bank Financial submitted to the court of first instance relevant litigation materials including a writ of summons and a judgment of the High Court of Hong Kong. Those materials indicated that on April 17, 2002, Agricultural Bank Financial filed a lawsuit in the High Court of Hong Kong against Junxing Company, Sanxing Axle Company, and its legal representative Xie Tiguang as defendants, seeking an order for the three defendants to repay the loan principal of USD 14,000,000 involved in this case and the overdue interest and handling fees as of March 22, 2002, totaling HKD 120,850,002.17. The High Court of Hong Kong rendered a civil judgment No. 1453 of 2002 on June 3, 2002, ordering Junxing Company to repay the above amounts claimed by Agricultural Bank Financial, namely USD 24,643,383.31 (or the equivalent in Hong Kong dollars at the time of repayment) and HKD 120,850,002.17, plus interest on those amounts from March 23, 2002 to the date of judgment (interest on the loan principal of USD 14,000,000 calculated at an annual rate of 12.125%, and interest on the letter of credit financing principal of HKD 67,992,581.32 calculated at an annual rate of 11.40%), and thereafter interest at the judgment rate until full payment.

The court of first instance held: Between the parties to this case, there exist a mortgage contract relationship based on the mortgage of land use rights and a guarantee contract relationship based on the irrevocable guarantees. Therefore, this case is a guarantee contract dispute. As Agricultural Bank Financial is a party from Hong Kong, this case is a Hong Kong-related case. Pursuant to Article 3, paragraphs (1) and (2) of the Supreme People's Court's "Reply on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Economic Dispute Cases Involving Hong Kong and Macao" regarding the application of law in Hong Kong and Macao-related cases, Hong Kong and Macao-related cases shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of China's mainland civil procedure law for foreign-related civil proceedings in terms of procedural matters, and in accordance with the provisions of China's mainland law on the application of law to foreign-related civil relations in terms of substantive matters. Therefore, this case shall be handled as a foreign-related case in terms of the application of law.

Although the various Mortgage Loan Agreements and Letter of Credit Financing Mortgage Agreements involved in this case contain provisions on choice of law and jurisdiction, it is clear that such choices were agreed between the borrower and the lender, not between the plaintiff and the defendant in this case. Therefore, the choice of law and jurisdiction clauses in the above agreements cannot serve as the basis for determining jurisdiction and the applicable law in this case. The domicile of the defendant Sanxing Axle Company is in Yangjiang City, Guangdong Province, which is within the jurisdiction of this court. Pursuant to Article 22, paragraph (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, which provides that a court at the defendant's domicile may exercise jurisdiction over contract disputes, this court has jurisdiction over the dispute in this case in accordance with the law. The parties in this case did not choose the law applicable to the mortgage contract relationship and the guarantee contract relationship. Pursuant to Article 145, paragraph (2) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, which provides that "where the parties to a foreign-related contract have not made a choice, the law of the country with which the contract is most closely connected shall be applied," the dispute in this case shall be governed by the law determined according to the principle of the closest connection. As the essential characteristic of a guarantee contract is reflected in the performance of the guarantor, i.e., the characteristic performance party of the guarantee contract is the guarantor, and the domicile of the guarantor Sanxing Axle Company in this case is in the mainland, both the mortgage contract relationship and the guarantee contract relationship have the closest connection with the mainland and therefore shall be governed by mainland law.

The mortgage and guarantee provided by the defendant Sanxing Axle Company to the plaintiff Agricultural Bank Financial, domiciled in Hong Kong, in the form of land use rights and irrevocable guarantees respectively, constitute external guarantees. As such external guarantee occurred after the implementation of the Guarantee Law of the PRC and was not subject to the corresponding approval and registration procedures with the mainland foreign exchange control authorities, pursuant to Article 133, paragraph (3) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the PRC, which provides that "for dispute cases arising from guarantee acts after the implementation of the Guarantee Law that are still in the first instance or second instance after the promulgation and implementation of this Interpretation, the Guarantee Law and this Interpretation shall apply," and Article 6, paragraph (1), which provides that external guarantee contracts that have not been approved or registered by the relevant competent state authorities are invalid, the mortgage contracts and guarantee contracts in this case shall be confirmed void in accordance with the law. Both Sanxing Axle Company and Agricultural Bank Financial, by providing and accepting the guarantee without the approval of the mainland foreign exchange control authorities, are at fault for the invalidity of the guarantee contracts. Pursuant to Article 7 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the PRC, where the principal contract is valid but the guarantee contract is invalid, "if both the creditor and the guarantor are at fault, the portion of civil liability borne by the guarantor shall not exceed one-half of the part that the debtor cannot repay." Accordingly, the guarantor Sanxing Axle Company shall bear compensation liability to the creditor Agricultural Bank Financial for one-half of the part that the debtor Junxing Company cannot repay. On April 17, 2002, Agricultural Bank Financial filed a lawsuit in the High Court of Hong Kong against Junxing Company, Sanxing Axle Company, and its legal representative Xie Tiguang as defendants. On June 3, 2002, the High Court of Hong Kong rendered a judgment ordering Junxing Company to repay the outstanding amounts of USD 24,643,383.31 and HKD 120,850,002.17, plus interest on those amounts. Therefore, the portion that Junxing Company cannot repay as of June 3, 2002 is USD 24,643,383.31 and HKD 120,850,002.17 plus interest. The court of first instance does not support Agricultural Bank Financial's claim seeking an order for Sanxing Axle Company to repay all principal and interest owed by Junxing Company and to exercise priority right in compensation from the land use rights involved in this case, nor does it support Sanxing Axle Company's defense that it should not bear liability. Agricultural Bank Financial filed its lawsuit with this court on July 7, 1998. The performance periods specified in the Mortgage Loan Agreements and Letter of Credit Financing Mortgage Agreements involved in this case had not exceeded two years as of the date of filing the lawsuit. Therefore, the court of first instance does not support Sanxing Axle Company's defense that the plaintiff's claim was time-barred. Since the guarantee contracts in this case are void, Sanxing Axle Company's defense based on the guarantee period does not constitute a valid defense, and the court of first instance does not support it.

Pursuant to Article 6, paragraph (1), Article 133, paragraph (3), and Article 7 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Sanxing Axle Company shall bear compensation liability to Agricultural Bank Financial for one-half of the part of the principal and interest owed by Junxing Company under the two Mortgage Loan Agreements and the two Letter of Credit Financing Mortgage Agreements involved in this case that cannot be repaid.

2. Other claims of Agricultural Bank Financial are dismissed.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of USD 92,435 and HKD 417,292.25 shall be borne equally by the plaintiff and the defendant. The pre-paid case acceptance fee shall not be refunded; when performing this judgment, Sanxing Axle Company shall directly pay USD 46,217.5 and HKD 208,646.1 to Agricultural Bank Financial.

Nongyin Company, dissatisfied with the original judgment, appealed to this Court, arguing: First, the Appellant had no fault in the invalidity of the guarantee contract, and Sanxing Axle Company should bear joint and several compensation liability for the debts that Junxing Company is unable to repay. The guarantee act of Sanxing Axle Company occurred in November and December 1995 and May 1996, and the "Administrative Measures for Domestic Institutions Providing Guarantees to Overseas" was not promulgated and implemented until September 1996. The external guarantee in this case cannot be governed by the "Administrative Measures for Domestic Institutions Providing Guarantees to Overseas" but should be governed by the "Administrative Measures for Domestic Institutions Providing Foreign Exchange Guarantees to Overseas" promulgated in September 1991. Article 10 of those Measures provides: After issuing a guarantee, the guarantor shall, within 10 days, go through the guarantee registration procedures with the local foreign exchange administration department. Thus, the registration procedures for external guarantees are handled by the guarantor and have nothing to do with the creditor. Nongyin Company had no fault in the invalidity of the guarantee contract in this case. Pursuant to Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, where the principal contract is valid but the security contract is invalid and the creditor is not at fault, the guarantor shall be jointly and severally liable for compensating the creditor's economic losses. Second, the mortgage in this case is legal and valid, and the Appellant, Nongyin Company, has a priority right to be satisfied from the mortgaged property. As mentioned above, this case should be governed by the "Administrative Measures for Domestic Institutions Providing Foreign Exchange Guarantees to Overseas" promulgated in September 1991. According to Article 2 of those Measures, external guarantees are limited to "suretyship" and do not include "mortgage" guarantees. Therefore, the mortgage in this case does not constitute an "external guarantee" and cannot be governed by the provision on invalidity of external guarantees in Article 6 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on the Security Law. The mortgaged property in this case has undergone mortgage registration procedures, and the mortgage contract is legal and valid. The court of first instance erred in holding the mortgage contract invalid and in applying the law, and this should be corrected. Accordingly, the Appellant requests that the judgment of first instance be set aside, that Sanxing Axle Company be ordered to bear joint and several compensation liability for the debts that Junxing Company is unable to repay, that Nongyin Company be recognized as having a priority right to be satisfied from the mortgaged property in this case, and that Sanxing Axle Company bear all litigation costs.

Sanxing Axle Company argued in defense: The guarantee issued by the Respondent to Nongyin Company on behalf of Junxing Company constitutes an external guarantee. Because the guarantee contract did not undergo approval and registration procedures, pursuant to Article 133, paragraph 3, and Article 6, item (1) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China, the guarantee contract in this case should be held invalid. The guarantor, Nongyin Company, is also at fault for causing the contract to be invalid. As the creditor, Nongyin Company had the obligation to ascertain whether the guarantor had the qualification to issue such a guarantee and whether approval or registration with the relevant department was required. Nongyin Company failed to fulfill its duty of care and accepted the guarantee; thus, it is also at fault for the invalidity of both the suretyship contract and the mortgage contract. The Respondent requests that Nongyin Company's appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

This Court holds that this case is a dispute over a guarantee contract involving Hong Kong. Because the mortgaged property under the mortgage contract in this case is located in the mainland and consists of immovable property, pursuant to Article 186 of this Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), civil relationships concerning the ownership, sale, lease, mortgage, and use of immovable property shall be governed by the law of the place where the immovable property is located. The court of first instance correctly applied Chinese law, and both parties have no objection to this, which should be confirmed.

The Appellant Nongyin Company's requests on appeal can be summarized into two main points: first, that the mortgage guarantee relationship in this case should be held valid; and second, that the Respondent Sanxing Company should bear joint and several compensation liability for the principal obligation in this case.

The then-effective "Administrative Measures for Domestic Institutions Providing Foreign Exchange Guarantees to Overseas" (approved by the People's Bank of China on August 1, 1991, and promulgated by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange on September 26, 1991) provided in Article 2: "For the purposes of these Measures, foreign exchange guarantee refers to the undertaking, made with one's own foreign exchange funds to an overseas creditor or a domestic foreign-funded bank, Sino-foreign joint venture bank, or foreign-funded or Sino-foreign joint venture non-bank financial institution, that when the debtor fails to repay the foreign exchange debt as stipulated in the contract, the guarantor will perform the obligation of repayment in foreign currency." Clearly, the scope of application of these Measures is guarantees made with one's own foreign exchange funds. However, the mortgage guarantee provided by Sanxing Axle Company was a guarantee for foreign exchange debts, and the performance of the guarantee liability would necessarily involve the issue of repaying debts in foreign exchange. According to the provisions of the "Administrative Measures for Domestic Institutions Providing Foreign Exchange Guarantees to Overseas," foreign exchange guarantees require examination, approval, management, and registration by the foreign exchange administration department. A foreign exchange guarantee that has not been approved violates China's foreign exchange control system and should be held invalid. In this regard, the judgment of first instance correctly held that the "Irrevocable Letter of Guarantee" issued by Sanxing Axle Company was invalid.

The mortgage guarantee act in this case occurred after the implementation of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China. After the mortgage contract is held invalid, the Security Law and this Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Judicial Interpretation on the Security Law) should be applied to determine the respective liabilities of the parties.

According to the provisions of the Judicial Interpretation on the Security Law, after the mortgage contract is held invalid, the liability between the parties shall be determined based on their respective degrees of fault. Because China implements a foreign exchange control system, and the administrative measures concerning foreign exchange guarantees are also publicly available, all parties should have known the laws and regulations of our country. The Appellant's argument that it was not at fault on the ground that the approval procedures should have been handled by the Respondent is untenable. If liability after the invalidity of the guarantee contract were determined solely based on who handled the approval procedures, then an overseas creditor could disregard China's foreign exchange control policies and regulations, and bear no liability due to the absence of fault, ultimately leading to a situation where, although the mortgage guarantee is invalid, the substantive outcome is the same as if the contract were valid. The court of first instance correctly held that Sanxing Axle Company and Nongyin Company were both at fault for the invalidity of the guarantee contract, having provided and accepted the guarantee without approval from the mainland foreign exchange administration department. Pursuant to Article 7 of the Judicial Interpretation on the Security Law, in cases where the principal contract is valid but the security contract is invalid, "if both the creditor and the guarantor are at fault, the portion of civil liability to be borne by the guarantor shall not exceed one-half of the portion of the debt that the debtor is unable to repay." Accordingly, the judgment of first instance, which ordered the guarantor Sanxing Axle Company to compensate the creditor Nongyin Company for one-half of the portion of the debt that debtor Junxing Company is unable to repay, is not improper.

In conclusion, the judgment of first instance has clear findings of fact and correctly applies the law. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court renders the following judgment:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The costs of the appeal, amounting to USD 92,435 and HKD 417,292.25, shall be borne by Nongyin Company.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Yun

Acting Judge: Yang Xingye
